title: start's host-setup warning does not fire on a rule gate whose wording only names a host
goal: backlog.py start and check warn of a gate naming a host setup with no --host-check only when the gate's options set something up on a host, not when the gate settles a rule's wording that mentions a loaded host; in SP-rlincemn ST-u24f5a2i's gate retry (how often a refused suite is rerun) drew the warning and needed gate host-unchecked
notes: Merged from ST-4yv2thhh “start's host-setup warning names the gate host-unchecked command” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: Premise holds: the host-setup warning text at _tools/bl_plan.py:368 names no gate host-unchecked command. It is the same warning in the same function as ST-dbyng654 (similar 1.00), so one commit covers both. Its goal: Found by the SP-qxcj7fgy review: ST-7avb5uo6 added backlog.py gate host-unchecked ID GATE --reason TEXT, but the start warning for a gate that names a host setup (bl_plan.py) still says only 'or the reason it cannot be checked as the gate's host_unchecked', never the command that sets it. The warning names gate host-unchecked ID GATE --reason TEXT. Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(0 if 'gate host-unchecked' in open('_tools/bl_plan.py',encoding='utf-8').read() else 1)"]} Its touches: _tools/bl_plan.py, kb/_self/backlog.md, kb/_self/tools.md Recurred SP-qlpfcgs2 start: gate load of ST-aqvuanq7 (a per-core load threshold) drew the host-setup warning; recorded as host_unchecked. Recurred at SP-uzwbt63u start (2026-10-13): BG-xp3imb24 g2 (the word credential in an option of a classing rule) and ST-webfvbcb g2 (the word host in host-check) drew the host-setup warning; both were answered design gates with no host setup.
